description: This line plot illustrates the training loss evolution over iterations for five different large language model configurations. The x-axis represents the number of iterations, labeled “#Iteration,” and spans from 0 to approximately 140,000 on a linear scale. The y-axis represents the loss value, labeled “Loss,” and ranges from approximately 2.4 to 3.4 on a linear scale. The plot contains five distinct lines: a purple line labeled “Vanilla,” a blue line labeled “StrmLLM (n=64),” an orange line labeled “SepLLM (n=64, H),” a green line labeled “SepLLM (n=64, H/T),” and a red line labeled “SepLLM (n=128).” All lines begin at a high loss value near 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a rapid initial decline before leveling off. The “Vanilla” line starts at a loss of approximately 3.4 and drops to about 2.7 by iteration 10,000, then stabilizes near 2.7. The “StrmLLM (n=64)” line starts at approximately 3.4 and declines to about 2.9 by iteration 10,000, then stabilizes near 2.9. The “SepLLM (n=64, H)” line starts at approximately 3.4 and declines to about 2.7 by iteration 10,000, then stabilizes near 2.7. The “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” line starts at approximately 3.4 and declines to about 2.7 by iteration 10,000, then stabilizes near 2.7. The “SepLLM (n=128)” line starts at approximately 3.4 and declines to about 2.7 by iteration 10,000, then stabilizes near 2.7. All lines exhibit some fluctuation around their final stable loss values.
